subject: Questions about scantwo/whole genome interaction scan

messages.author: 6ac703b057276f22
messages.subject: Questions about scantwo/whole genome interaction scan
parts:
I am conducting a QTL mapping study looking at seed phenotypes in RIL
populations. I am familiar with the literature in the subject area,
but am very new to R/qtl and with so many possibilities, I do not know
which scripts to choose. I have already detected robust QTL with CIM
using both QTL cartographer and Rqtl. Now I am conducting a two-
dimensional, two-QTL genome scan to detect linked loci. This is where
I've run into problems.

Mapmanager was used to detect epistatic interactions. I then
performed linear regression phenotype on marker genotype to validate
interactions. My PI decided that reviewers would prefer to see work
done in R/QTL so I switched platforms. However, the script I've been
using for scantwo continually detects false interactions and fail to
pick up minor loci that I know to interact.

Scantwo only returns large composite QTL that I know do not interact.
I have tried all three methods (imp, hk, em). I went back and put in
a model based on known interactions (validated in BC1 and with JMP LS
Mean analysis) and it called all my interactions as NS except the ones
called by Scantwo. There must be a problem with my script or my
logic, but I am at a loss. Is there a standard script/pipeline to
use? Is there a way to do linear regression phenotype on marker
genotype for all loci like statistical analysis software does for
marker pairs?

Any input/suggestions are greatly appreciated. Thanks!

SCRIPTS I've tried:

library(qtl)
d1 <- read.cross("csv",dir="/Users/Diana/
Desktop",file="RQTL_INP_DBW.csv", genotypes = c("A", "B"))
d1riself <- convert2riself(d1)
d1riself.newmap <- est.map(d1riself, error.prob = .001, map.function =
c("haldane"))
d1riself <- replace.map(d1riself, d1riself.newmap)
d1riself <- calc.genoprob(d1riself, step=1, error.prob=0.01)


#scantwo pheno1
operm1 <- scantwo(d1riself, pheno.col=1, method="hk", n.perm=1000)
summary(operm1)
out1 <- scantwo(d1riself, pheno.col=1, method="hk")
summary(out1, perms=operm1, alphas=c(0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05),
pvalues=TRUE)
plot(clean(out1))

#fitqtl
d1riself.sim <- sim.geno(d1riself, n.draws=200, step=0, off.end=0,
error.prob=0.0001, map.function=c("haldane"),stepwidth=c("fixed"))
qtl <- makeqtl(d1riself.sim, chr=c(1,1,2,3,4,5), pos=c(1, 120, 60, 41,
64, 4 ))
lod <- fitqtl(d1riself.sim, pheno.col=1, method=c("imp"), qtl=qtl,
formula=y~Q1+Q2+Q3+Q4+Q5+Q6+Q1:Q4+Q3:Q5+Q4:Q6+Q4:Q5)
